newsitem.title: UK: Big shareholders undecided on bid - Clyde.
newsitem.headline: Big shareholders undecided on bid - Clyde.

text.p: Clyde Petroleum said its major shareholders were undecided whether to accept Gulf Canada's 432 million stg hostile offer amid market speculation that a counter bidder may emerge.

"I have not talked to any shareholder who is prepared to accept this offer," said Clyde chairman Malcolm Gourlay, reacting to industry sources who earlier told Reuters that major shareholders might be willing to accept the bid if no white knight appeared.
"Nobody would take a view on what bid should be accepted at this stage," Gourlay told Reuters.
Gourlay reiterated that Gulf's 105 pence per share offer was inadequate and seriously undervalued Clyde.
"We remain absolutely resolute that this offer is totally inadequate," he said.
Gourlay also lashed out at Gulf's earlier comments that Clyde's defence, released on Sunday, was "thin soup" without much substantial new information.
"To say there was no material new information is extremely thin. Record reserves, a new gas project and a very full drilling programme in 1997: that was material new information," Gourlay said.
In its defence document, Clyde said commercial reserves are estimated to rise by 21 percent to a record 130 million barrels of oil equivalent at end 1996.
The company also announced a new near-term project -- the West Natuna Gas project in Indonesia -- and said its 1997 exploration and appraisal programme would include drilling a total 100 wells.
One analyst told Reuters earlier that he believed it was unlikely Clyde would be taken over for less than 125 pence per share.
Clyde shares closed down 1/2p at 117 pence.
